newsitem.title: UK: TREG extends offer for KEPIT.
newsitem.headline: TREG extends offer for KEPIT.

text.p: TR European Growth Trust (TREG) said on Friday it had extended its offer for the Kleinwort European Privatisation Trust Plc (KEPIT) and challenged KEPIT's board to better its offer, which it said valued KEPIT shares at "up to 101.5 pence".

"The TREG Board is confident that its cash offer is more attractive than that offered by KEPIT," TREG said in a statement, adding that it had negotiated an exclusive rate for a programme trade of the KEPIT portfolio "at under half the cost of competitive bids obtained in the market".
TREG said it was extending its offer for KEPIT until October 4, 1996 and the level of acceptances received at the first closing date would be announced on September 16.

"If the KEPIT proposals can beat our cash offer, KEPIT investors have been well served. If they cannot, the KEPIT board should recommend our offers immediately," Sir Geoffrey Littler, TREG's chairman said.

TREG said KEPIT should provide estimates of what their cash exit would be worth on the basis that between 70 and 90 percent of investors would seek this. "This will enable the KEPIT investor to make a valid comparison," it added.

TREG said its cash offer valued each KEPIT ordinary share at 97.3 pence, the offer value per KEPIT warrant is 29.2 pence and the offer value per unit of one share and one-fifth warrant is 103.1 pence.

It said the benefits of its programme trade outweigh the 10 million stg cost savings identified by KEPIT's own proposals "which is why the TREG board believes it it offering greater cash value than KEPIT's unitisation".
